clue.text: Leave one's hotel to investigate

definitions.meaning: to settle the bill and depart from a hotel at the end of a stay
to look into something and verify it

explanation.surface: A guest is told to leave the hotel in order to look into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday phrasal verbs: departing a hotel formally, and examining something closely to verify it.

clue.text: Fight taking one second on average

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for a second of time
par is the normal or average level, as in 'up to par'

explanation.surface: A boxer takes a single second in an otherwise ordinary bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight, especially in practice or in a light exchange of blows.

clue.text: Cosmopolitan city quarter

parts.note: urban means belonging to a city
E, east, is one of the four compass points or quarters

explanation.surface: A particular district of a city is described as cosmopolitan.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and worldly, a close synonym of cosmopolitan in the sense of polished sophistication.

clue.text: Is embraced by a longing for a sweet

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a need is a longing or craving
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a craving for something sweet finds it wrapped in longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like an adjective but is the noun: aniseed balls are a traditional British boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed ball is a traditional hard sweet, so aniseed names a confection here as well as a flavouring.

clue.text: Order dessert

definitions.meaning: ... order means perfect neatness, so the phrase stands for order
a pudding of baked apples in pastry

explanation.surface: A diner asks for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order is an idiom for perfect tidiness, and the pie itself is a classic dessert.

clue.text: What drivers should avoid — and what passes through it

definitions.meaning: a narrow stretch of road where traffic jams build up
the narrow top of a bottle, through which the drink is poured

explanation.surface: Advice to motorists about a hazard, with a teasing nod to something flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a traffic choke point and, literally, the narrow neck of a bottle that liquid flows through.

clue.text: Could be posted to headquarters

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: An officer might be posted to headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Depots are military bases or headquarters where regiments are stationed and stores held.

clue.text: Young female accompanist

parts.note: read not as a pianist who is young and female but as a person who accompanies a young woman for propriety

explanation.surface: A girl who plays piano for a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an older person escorting a young unmarried woman in public to ensure proper behaviour.

clue.text: Searched for a resting place

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
a bed is somewhere to rest

explanation.surface: Someone hunted around for somewhere to lie down.
explanation.definitionFit: To have probed is to have searched or investigated thoroughly.

clue.text: Cliff shows where he was hurt

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky face of a hill
a mark left on the skin after a wound has healed

explanation.surface: A man points to the cliff where he had his accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Scar is a northern English word for a cliff or rocky outcrop, and also the mark a healed wound leaves.

clue.text: A bishop has the answer — forgiveness

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A bishop offers forgiveness as the answer to sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal forgiveness of sins pronounced by a priest.

clue.text: Go looking for a scrap when surrounded by the enemy

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed by another, so it goes inside

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A soldier hunts for food while hemmed in by hostile forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food or provisions.

clue.text: Sign for a missing letter

parts.note: read not as a notice about lost post but as the punctuation mark showing where a letter has been omitted

explanation.surface: A notice posted about a lost piece of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark in contractions like 'don't' stands in for an omitted letter.

clue.text: When sprees turn out thus, strong coffee is required

indicators.note: the letters turn out differently, signalling an anagram

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: After nights out on a spree, a strong coffee is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' is not a link word here; it gives letters of its own after the shuffled sprees.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong concentrated coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Gave support or just watched?

explanation.surface: A question of whether a friend helped or merely looked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both remained loyal to someone and stayed passively on the sidelines.

clue.text: Support the team that's bottom

parts.note: to back is to support
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Fans are urged to support the team at the foot of the league.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside is an informal word for the buttocks, i.e. one's bottom.

clue.text: Lease in legal document taken out

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
to let is to lease property

explanation.surface: A lease is contained in a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted means removed or struck out from a text.

clue.text: He's bound to better himself elsewhere

definitions.text: He's bound to better himself elsewhere

parts.words: He's bound to better himself elsewhere
parts.note: bound here means heading for a destination, not obliged: a man travelling abroad for a better life

explanation.surface: A man is certain to do well somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaving his country to settle in another, often for better prospects, is a person who moves abroad permanently.

clue.text: Girl able to turn up on a whole lot of dates

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: can means be able to

explanation.surface: A capable girl is expected to show up on several dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses CAN to NAC, written under ALMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly calendar listing dates and events, humorously a whole lot of dates.

clue.text: Poor clot breaks the rules of etiquette

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool commits a breach of manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal code of correct conduct on official or ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Jack, the tearaway?

parts.note: suggests a wild youth called Jack, but points to the Victorian murderer's byname read as one who tears

explanation.surface: A boy named Jack is a young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper was the notorious Victorian killer, and a ripper is literally one who tears.

clue.text: Contract to accommodate lodgers

definitions.meaning: to make smaller or narrower, as with a garment
to give paying guests rooms in one's home

explanation.surface: An agreement is drawn up for housing tenants.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to make a garment narrower and also to house paying guests.

clue.text: Bound to have a prior engagement

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to have another appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally fastened with cord and also busy or occupied with other commitments.

clue.text: Ideal setting for production of Pinafore?

definitions.text: Ideal setting for production of Pinafore?

parts.words: Ideal setting for production of Pinafore?
parts.note: suggests a theatre for the operetta HMS Pinafore, but a pinafore is a kind of overall worn over clothes

explanation.surface: A drama critic wonders which venue best suits the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; a pinafore is also an apron-like garment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the part of a theatre stage projecting in front of the curtain, named after the garment.

clue.text: It's unusual to return right on time

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is uncommon to come back right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; 'on' places the time-word after right in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom occurring, which is to say unusual.

clue.text: We hear old area of land is uncultivated

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a rood is an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre

explanation.surface: We are told an ancient plot of land lies wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in an older sense means rough, primitive and unrefined, i.e. uncultivated.

clue.text: A way of acting part of Hamlet's madness

definitions.meaning: the naturalistic acting technique associated with Stanislavski
Polonius says of Hamlet 'Though this be madness

explanation.surface: An actor describes one approach to playing Hamlet's feigned insanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Method acting is a famous technique, and Polonius's line gives the idiom of order within apparent madness.

clue.text: Plentiful supply coming from British sailor and German worker

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a British sailor
und is the German word for and
an ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords

explanation.surface: A large supply arrives from a British seaman and a German labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means existing in large quantities, a straightforward synonym of plentiful.
